proposal.summary: Multiple DrayTek products use hardcoded encryption keys in certain firmware/app versions, allowing attackers to bind affected devices to attacker-controlled accounts and create/synchronize WCF and DrayDDNS licenses from the website.
proposal.affected_product: Draytek Vigor Routers (firmware < 3.9.6/4.2.4), Access Points (firmware < v1.4.0), Switches (firmware < 2.6.7), Myvigor (firmware < 2.3.2)
proposal.cwe_quote: were discovered to use hardcoded encryption keys

AV.quote: were discovered to use hardcoded encryption keys which allows attackers to bind any affected device to their own account.

PR.quote: which allows attackers to bind any affected device to their own account.

C.quote: Attackers are then able to create WCF and DrayDDNS licenses and synchronize them from the website.

I.quote: Attackers are then able to create WCF and DrayDDNS licenses and synchronize them from the website.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Request reproduction details and proof-of-concept from reporter (how keys are used, required network access, and exact impact), and confirm whether account binding and license creation/actions are possible remotely without authentication.
